entry.title: An Unbounded Gap Between Identification and Identifiable Elicitation: Central Moments
entry.summary: For $n\geq2$, two expectation equations identify the mean together with the $n$th central moment. How many coordinates must a report have if a one-observation loss uniquely elicits it and the report determines that moment? We prove that $n$ coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries. The result holds on every open convex set of positive distributions on any $n+1$ distinct real outcomes. It requires no regularity of the loss, report map, identification function, or link. Thus $\operatorname{elic}_{\mathcal I}(μ_n)=n$ while $\operatorname{iden}(μ_n)\leq2$, giving an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification. This resolves the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash on the stated domains. The proof constructs a $C^1$ manifold of supporting coefficients from the affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk. Translations along that manifold force an $n$-dimensional tangent space. Standardized moments of order at least three have the same exact complexity. The bound also extends to convex distribution classes with a full-dimensional raw-moment image.

entry.title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
entry.summary: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

entry.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
entry.summary: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles. Using a direct Gegenbauer-moment proof and a continuant comparison criterion, we show that the row polynomials form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence for every real $θ\ge0$, and establish the same property for the moment sequences associated with all tails of the corresponding Jacobi matrix. Their $γ$-expansion, real-rootedness and Stieltjes moment representation are explicit, as are the exact orders of vanishing and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. This confirms and strengthens Rodelet--Causse--Tevlin's log-convexity conjecture for super Narayana polynomials. We further extend Wang--Yang's total positivity of the type~$A$ and $B$ Narayana triangles and strict total positivity of the associated squares to every real $θ>-1$, using Pólya-frequency sequences and a gamma-product moment representation. We also prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every $θ\ge0$, and that every $d$-Hoggatt transformation has the same property for integers $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs employ the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument based on a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.

entry.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
entry.summary: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cramér's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.

entry.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for Rényi Entropy
entry.summary: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for Rényi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

entry.title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
entry.summary: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Małecki and Żak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.

entry.title: A polynomial bound in Dvoretzky's theorem
entry.summary: We present a simple proof of the $\varepsilon$-Dvoretzky conjecture, which asserts that the dependence on the approximation parameter $\varepsilon$ in Dvoretzky's theorem is polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. In particular, if $n \geq (C/\varepsilon)^{\ell/2+1}$, then any $n$-dimensional convex body has, through any given interior point, an $\ell$-dimensional section that is $\varepsilon$-close to a Euclidean ball. Here, $C > 0$ is a universal constant. We in fact obtain a sharper dependence on $\varepsilon$. The proof is probabilistic, but uses a different probabilistic model from those employed previously. We also prove a simultaneous version of our theorem for a finite family of convex bodies with the origin in their interior, yielding a common linear subspace on which all of the bodies have nearly-Euclidean sections. Finally, we compare the radius of the approximating Euclidean ball with familiar geometric parameters, such as the mean widths of the body and its dual.

entry.title: Negative Correlations for Forests and the $q<1$ Random Cluster Model
entry.summary: We study negative edge correlation for two well-known models in statistical physics, the arboreal gas and the $q < 1$ random-cluster model. We show that after the edges $e$ and $f$ are removed, their Rayleigh difference is a crossing contribution minus the covariance of two endpoint-connectivity events. For the arboreal gas on an arbitrary finite graph, we analyze the two leading coefficients of this difference. The first is the classical transfer-current square. If it vanishes, the second has an electrical sum-of-squares formula. This proves negative edge correlation at sufficiently large fugacity whenever one of the two leading coefficients of the Rayleigh difference is nonzero, and characterizes simultaneous equality by an equipotential decomposition. For the random-cluster model on the complete graph $K_n$, we prove negative edge correlation throughout $q<1$ when all edge weights are at least $2$. In the uniform case, we prove something stronger:negative correlation holds when all the weights are equal and at least $1$. In particular, distinct edges in a connected spanning subgraph of $K_n$, weighted by a fixed fugacity, are negatively correlated for every $n$. We also explore what seems to be a general phenomenon: positive correlation of connectivity events. For the arboreal gas, we prove positive correlation for connectivity events at high fugacities. On lattices, the conjectured inequality would make the two-point function supermultiplicative and produce a convex inverse correlation length. Exact computations support the graph and matroid conjectures, including the Seymour--Welsh matroid $\mathcal S_8$, where ordinary edge-negative correlation fails. The results in this paper were derived by the authors without the use of Large Language models. The authors did benefit from using GPT-5 Pro for generating code to test out hypotheses as well as for simplifying the arguments.

entry.title: Singularity of harmonic measures for hyperbolic lattices
entry.summary: Let $Γ<\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb H^n)$, $n\geq2$, be a cocompact lattice containing a convex cocompact codimension-one subgroup in the sense of Sageev. We prove that every finitely supported admissible random walk on $Γ$ has hitting measure singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\partial\mathbb H^n$. The proof extends the method of Kosenko--Tiozzo, replacing Fourier analysis for a cyclic subgroup by a von Neumann dimension argument that also applies to nonabelian subgroups. As corollaries, we prove the singularity conjecture of Kaimanovich and Le Prince for cocompact hyperbolic lattices admitting a proper cocompact cubulation, cocompact Kleinian groups, and cocompact hyperbolic lattices with totally geodesic sublattices of codimension one. In particular, our result covers all cocompact hyperbolic reflection groups, cocompact arithmetic lattices of simplest type and cocompact nonarithmetic lattices arising from the hybrid and inbreeding constructions.

entry.title: The Sharp Rényi and Tsallis Threshold in the Shepp--Olkin Concavity Problem
entry.summary: Let $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ be independent Bernoulli random variables with parameters $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, and let $S=\sum_i B_i$. Hillion and Johnson proved that the Shannon entropy of $S$ is jointly concave in the parameter vector and proposed corresponding critical-order conjectures for R'enyi and Tsallis entropies, with predicted thresholds $2$ and approximately $3.65986$, respectively. We determine both thresholds exactly. For every $0<q<1$, the power sum $\sum_k \mathbb P(S=k)^q$ is jointly concave in $(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, and strictly concave on the open parameter cube. Consequently, the R'enyi and Tsallis entropies of order $q$ are jointly concave. At $q=1$ this agrees with the Shannon theorem. For every $q>1$, joint concavity fails already for the sum of two Bernoulli variables: a transverse interpolation in which the two parameters move in opposite directions gives strict local convexity for both entropies. Hence the universal joint-concavity range for both families is exactly $0<q\leq 1$. Below order one, the proof combines the Hillion--Johnson transport inequality with an explicit nonlinear telescoping correction. The corrected local curvature reduces to a two-dimensional quadratic form. An exact Riccati identity, together with a one-sided zero-crossing argument, proves positivity of its determinant throughout the full range $0<q<1$.
